**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** on the exact proposal. The additive mapped-role architecture is sound and approved in direction, but the design is not yet implementable without ambiguity at three load-bearing points.

The top finding is at the CLI and consumer surface: the CLI hardcodes the legacy `source-static-unproven-uninstalled` status and the existing RED FeePool consumer asserts exactly that text while invoking `--authorization unsigned`, so the design as written would either leave the one RED test red or make it pass under a misleading qualification. It must explicitly migrate the consumer and README to `--authorization unsigned-mapped-roles`, derive the status line from the selected mode, pin the `debit_sources` definition (debit `from` rows only, sorted, always serialized) and mapped-mode error codes, pin the new manifest `compiler_hash` coverage, pin `pub(crate)` visibility and the deserializer arm, specify the coherent-fixture pattern for the native early-refusal tests, and refresh its recorded HEAD.

Everything else verified clean against the full current production chain: the `one-public-payer` failure is real (QA is 6 PASS / 1 RED), the funded FeePool source stays intact, native custody is genuinely single-owner so the strict guard must remain, every native and signed consumer recompiles strictly before any decode, VM, `k`, key, or proof work, the proposed refusal tests terminate before any forbidden SDK work under empty inputs, and all ten design-pinned compiler hashes still match at the new HEAD (`9c4dce45`, which committed the FeePool consumer during this review). Native authority remains zero and full M1–M17/U0–U7 remains open.

The full audit is written to [muse-mapped-role-design-review.md](/home/charl/Moriarty/.moriarty-dev/runtime/language-wave1-20261014/fee-pool/muse-mapped-role-design-review.md) with its companion [muse-mapped-role-design-review.json](/home/charl/Moriarty/.moriarty-dev/runtime/language-wave1-20261014/fee-pool/muse-mapped-role-design-review.json); no source files were edited and no tests or native work were executed.
